newsitem.title: USA: States, utilities to sue U.S. DOE on nuclear waste.
newsitem.headline: States, utilities to sue U.S. DOE on nuclear waste.

text.p: More than 40 state agencies and a coalition of 25 electric utilities will sue the U.S. Energy Department over its continued failure to accept spent fuel from nuclear reactors, spokesmen for the parties said Wednesday.

The lawsuit is partly in response to a letter the Energy Department sent to electric utilities in December saying it would not be able to start accepting the spent fuel by January 31, 1998, as scheduled, the utilities and state agencies said in a news release.

A spokesman said this lawsuit will be filed by basically the same parties that sued the Energy Department earlier over its failure to accept the waste as called for by the Nuclear Waste Policy Act of 1982.
The U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia in July ruled that the government must start disposing of nuclear waste from commercial reactors in 1998.

But the Energy Department, which does not yet have a central waste disposal site, in a letter in December said it could not meet that deadline, and said it would work with utilities to deal with the problem of the spent fuel accumulating at reactors around the country.

More information on the latest lawsuit is to be released at a news conference Thursday by Michigan Attorney General Frank Kelley and Kris Sanda, commissioner of Minnesota's Public Service Department and co-founder of the Nuclear Waste Strategy Coalition, according to the news release.
